subject: ela
intro: Informative writing explains a topic clearly using facts, definitions, and details. It introduces the topic, organizes ideas, develops them with relevant evidence, links ideas with transitions, keeps a formal tone, and ends with a conclusion that follows from the information. In each item below, read the short stimulus and identify the feature of informative writing that is asked for.

items.prompt:
A student is writing an informative article titled 'How Honeybees Make Honey.' Which opening sentence best introduces the topic for an informative text?
A) Honeybees turn flower nectar into honey through several steps inside the hive.
B) Everyone should plant more flowers to help the honeybees.
C) I think honey tastes better than any other food in the world.
D) One sunny day, a curious bee landed right on my arm.
items.answer: Honeybees turn flower nectar into honey through several steps inside the hive.

steps: An informative introduction names the topic and previews what the text will explain, using an objective, factual tone.
Choice A clearly states the topic (how honeybees make honey) and signals that steps will follow, so it is the best introduction.
Choice B states an opinion and tries to persuade. Choice C states a personal opinion. Choice D begins a personal story, none of which introduce informative content.
The best introductory sentence is: Honeybees turn flower nectar into honey through several steps inside the hive.

items.prompt:
Read this informative paragraph about volcanoes:
'A volcano is an opening in the Earth's surface. Hot melted rock called magma rises up through this opening. My family visited a beach last summer. When magma reaches the surface, it is called lava.'
Which sentence should be removed because it does not develop the topic?
A) A volcano is an opening in the Earth's surface.
B) Hot melted rock called magma rises up through this opening.
C) My family visited a beach last summer.
D) When magma reaches the surface, it is called lava.
items.answer: My family visited a beach last summer.

steps: Every sentence in an informative paragraph should develop the topic, which here is volcanoes.
Choices A, B, and D all give facts about volcanoes, magma, and lava.
Choice C is a personal detail about a beach trip that does not explain anything about volcanoes, so it should be removed.
The sentence that should be removed is: My family visited a beach last summer.

items.prompt:
Choose the transition that best fits the relationship between these two sentences:
'Most reptiles lay eggs. ______ some snakes give birth to live young.'
A) However,
B) In addition,
C) As a result,
D) For example,

steps: The first sentence says most reptiles lay eggs; the second gives an exception, so the relationship is contrast.
'However' signals a contrast, which fits a statement that goes against the general rule.
'In addition' signals adding more of the same idea, 'As a result' signals cause and effect, and 'For example' signals an illustration, none of which fit a contrast.
The correct transition is: However,

items.prompt:
Which sentence is written in a formal, objective tone appropriate for an informative text about bats?
A) Bats are nocturnal animals that hunt for insects at night.
B) Bats are super creepy and kind of freak me out.
C) Honestly, bats are the coolest animals you will ever see.
D) Bats are awesome little night creatures, no joke.
items.answer: Bats are nocturnal animals that hunt for insects at night.

steps: Informative writing uses a formal, objective tone and avoids slang or personal feelings.
Choice A states a fact about bats using precise, neutral language.
Choices B, C, and D use casual, emotional words like 'creepy,' 'coolest,' and 'no joke,' which are too informal for an informative text.
The formal sentence is: Bats are nocturnal animals that hunt for insects at night.

items.prompt:
A student is writing about the water cycle. Which sentence is the best concluding sentence for an informative paragraph that explained how water evaporates, forms clouds, and falls as rain?
A) In these ways, water moves between the Earth and the sky in a repeating cycle.
B) My favorite kind of weather is a warm, sunny day.
C) Did you know that some deserts almost never get any rain?
D) Clouds can also be many different shapes and colors.
items.answer: In these ways, water moves between the Earth and the sky in a repeating cycle.

steps: A concluding sentence should summarize and follow from the information already presented.
Choice A restates the main idea that water moves through a repeating cycle, which matches the paragraph.
Choice B states a personal opinion, and Choices C and D add brand-new information not discussed in the paragraph.
The best conclusion is: In these ways, water moves between the Earth and the sky in a repeating cycle.

items.prompt:
A draft sentence reads: 'The thing that pushes blood around your body works all day and night.' Which revision uses precise, domain-specific vocabulary for an informative text?
A) The heart pumps blood throughout the body all day and night.
B) That body part that does the blood stuff never stops working.
C) The blood pusher inside you keeps going nonstop.
D) The thing in your chest is always busy moving blood.
items.answer: The heart pumps blood throughout the body all day and night.

steps: Informative writing uses precise, domain-specific terms instead of vague phrases.
Choice A names the exact organ, the heart, and uses the accurate verb 'pumps.'
Choices B, C, and D all keep vague wording like 'blood stuff,' 'blood pusher,' or 'the thing,' which is imprecise.
The precise revision is: The heart pumps blood throughout the body all day and night.

items.prompt:
A student is writing an informative report titled 'The Life Cycle of a Butterfly.' Which sentence best introduces this topic?
A) A butterfly goes through four main stages as it grows from an egg into an adult.
B) Butterflies are the prettiest insects, and everyone agrees they are the best.
C) I once chased a butterfly across my whole backyard.
D) You really should learn about butterflies because they are amazing.
items.answer: A butterfly goes through four main stages as it grows from an egg into an adult.

steps: A topic-introduction sentence names the subject and previews what the report will cover, in a factual tone.
Choice A states the topic (the butterfly life cycle) and previews that there are four stages.
Choice B states an opinion, Choice C is a personal story, and Choice D tries to persuade the reader.
The best introduction is: A butterfly goes through four main stages as it grows from an egg into an adult.

items.prompt:
Read this informative paragraph about the moon:
'The moon is Earth's only natural satellite. It orbits the Earth about once every month. I really hope I can be an astronaut someday. The moon has no air or liquid water on its surface.'
Which sentence should be removed because it does not develop the topic?
A) The moon is Earth's only natural satellite.
B) It orbits the Earth about once every month.
C) I really hope I can be an astronaut someday.
D) The moon has no air or liquid water on its surface.
items.answer: I really hope I can be an astronaut someday.

steps: Each sentence should give information about the topic, which is the moon.
Choices A, B, and D all state facts about the moon.
Choice C shares a personal hope about being an astronaut and does not develop facts about the moon, so it should be removed.
The sentence that should be removed is: I really hope I can be an astronaut someday.

items.prompt:
Choose the transition that best fits the relationship between these two sentences:
'Penguins cannot fly. ______ they are excellent swimmers.'
A) However,
B) As a result,
C) In addition,
D) Before that,

steps: The two ideas contrast: penguins cannot fly, but they are still excellent at something (swimming).
'However' signals this contrast between a weakness and a strength.
'As a result' signals cause and effect, 'In addition' signals adding a similar idea, and 'Before that' signals time order, none of which fit the contrast.
The correct transition is: However,

items.prompt:
A topic sentence reads: 'Recycling helps protect the environment.' Which fact best develops and supports this topic sentence?
A) Recycling one ton of paper saves about seventeen trees and a large amount of water.
B) My neighborhood picks up recycling every Tuesday morning.
C) The color of most recycling bins in our town is blue.
D) I forgot to take out the recycling last week.
items.answer: Recycling one ton of paper saves about seventeen trees and a large amount of water.

steps: Supporting evidence should directly develop the topic sentence, which is that recycling protects the environment.
Choice A gives a fact showing an environmental benefit of recycling (saving trees and water), so it supports the topic.
Choices B and C give details about pickup days and bin color, which do not show environmental protection, and Choice D is a personal anecdote.
The best supporting fact is: Recycling one ton of paper saves about seventeen trees and a large amount of water.

items.prompt:
Which sentence is written in a formal, objective tone appropriate for an informative text about earthquakes?
A) An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement deep in the Earth.
B) Earthquakes are totally scary and they freak everybody out.
C) Whoa, earthquakes are the wildest thing ever, trust me.
D) Honestly, I would be so terrified during a big earthquake.
items.answer: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement deep in the Earth.

steps: An informative text uses formal, factual language and avoids slang and personal feelings.
Choice A defines an earthquake with precise, neutral wording.
Choices B, C, and D use casual or emotional words such as 'scary,' 'whoa,' 'wildest,' and 'terrified.'
The formal sentence is: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement deep in the Earth.

items.prompt:
A student wrote an informative paragraph explaining how plants use sunlight, water, and air to make food. Which sentence is the best concluding sentence?
A) Together, these parts allow a plant to make its own food and grow.
B) Roses and sunflowers are two flowers many people like to grow.
C) Some plants can also live underwater in lakes and rivers.
D) I think gardening is a really fun hobby to try.
items.answer: Together, these parts allow a plant to make its own food and grow.

steps: A concluding sentence should follow from and sum up the information already explained.
Choice A restates the main idea that the parts work together to help a plant make food and grow.
Choices B and C introduce new information not covered in the paragraph, and Choice D states a personal opinion.
The best conclusion is: Together, these parts allow a plant to make its own food and grow.

items.prompt:
A draft sentence reads: 'The cold, white stuff that falls from the sky covers the ground in winter.' Which revision uses precise, domain-specific vocabulary for an informative text?
A) Snow covers the ground during the winter months.
B) The frozen sky flakes pile up when it gets cold outside.
C) That white winter stuff comes down and sticks around.
D) The cold sky powder builds up on the ground in winter.
items.answer: Snow covers the ground during the winter months.

steps: Precise informative writing names things with their exact terms instead of vague descriptions.
Choice A uses the accurate word 'snow' to name what is being described.
Choices B, C, and D keep vague phrases like 'frozen sky flakes,' 'white winter stuff,' and 'cold sky powder.'
The precise revision is: Snow covers the ground during the winter months.

items.prompt:
Read this informative paragraph about spiders:
'Spiders are small animals with eight legs. Many spiders spin webs to catch insects for food. Spiders are not insects because insects have only six legs. Spiders are my least favorite animal of all.'
Which sentence should be removed because it does not develop the topic?
A) Spiders are small animals with eight legs.
B) Many spiders spin webs to catch insects for food.
C) Spiders are not insects because insects have only six legs.
D) Spiders are my least favorite animal of all.
items.answer: Spiders are my least favorite animal of all.

steps: Each sentence in an informative paragraph should give facts about the topic, which is spiders.
Choices A, B, and C all give factual information about spiders.
Choice D states a personal opinion ('least favorite') rather than a fact, so it should be removed.
The sentence that should be removed is: Spiders are my least favorite animal of all.

items.prompt:
Choose the transition that best fits the relationship between these two sentences:
'A solid has a fixed shape. ______ a liquid takes the shape of its container.'
A) However,
B) For example,
C) As a result,
D) Finally,

steps: The two sentences contrast a property of solids with a different property of liquids.
'However' signals this contrast between two opposite behaviors.
'For example' signals an illustration, 'As a result' signals cause and effect, and 'Finally' signals the last step in a sequence, none of which fit the contrast.
The correct transition is: However,
